description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Cost and Reliability Score for three different models: 3-Model Ensemble, 2-Model Ensemble, and GPT-4. The x-axis is labeled "Cost" and features a linear scale ranging from 0 to 10, with tick marks at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Reliability Score" and uses a linear scale ranging from 30 to 90, with tick marks at intervals of 20 and horizontal grid lines at 50, 70, and 90. The 3-Model Ensemble is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at a Reliability Score of approximately 82 at a Cost of 0, declines slightly to roughly 79 at a Cost of 5, and ends at approximately 75 at a Cost of 10. The 2-Model Ensemble is depicted by a solid red line with circular markers, starting at a Reliability Score of approximately 85 at a Cost of 0, decreasing to roughly 79 at a Cost of 5, and concluding at approximately 73 at a Cost of 10. Finally, GPT-4 is shown as a solid yellow line with circular markers, beginning at a Reliability Score of approximately 89 at a Cost of 0, experiencing a steep decline to roughly 65 at a Cost of 5, and finishing at approximately 41 at a Cost of 10.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the relationship between cost and reliability score for three distinct models: the 3-Model Ensemble, 2-Model Ensemble, and GPT-4. The x-axis is labeled 'Cost,' ranging from 0 to 10, while the y-axis is labeled 'Reliability Score,' spanning 30 to 90. The 3-Model Ensemble (blue line) begins at approximately 85 reliability at a cost of 0 and decreases steadily to around 75 at a cost of 10. The 2-Model Ensemble (red line) starts at roughly 88 reliability and exhibits a sharper decline, reaching approximately 70 at a cost of 10. GPT-4 (yellow line) begins at 90 reliability but shows the most pronounced drop, falling to approximately 50 at a cost of 10. Notably, the 2-Model Ensemble consistently outperforms the 3-Model Ensemble across all cost levels, while GPT-4 demonstrates a rapid decline in reliability after a cost of 2, intersecting the ensemble models at higher costs.
